# ResizeGripper

Header: `winui/ui/panes/ResizeGripper.hpp`. Spec: `winui/ui/panes/ResizeGripper.hpp`.

A fixed-size corner drag handle that reports two-axis deltas while dragged.

It draws three diagonal rows of dots anchored to its bottom-right corner, shows the diagonal resize cursor, and measures to a [`size()`](#size) square whatever it is offered. It resizes nothing itself. The app applies each (dx, dy) to whatever should grow, typically a [Grid](grid.md#uigrid) row and column or an element's explicit size. It works with the mouse only and never takes focus. For a single-axis pane splitter use [`Splitter`](splitter.md#uisplitter). [`ui::ResizeGripper`](#uiresizegripper) is the declarative form.

Example: 
```cpp
auto stack = std::make_unique<ui::StackControl>(ui::Orientation::Vertical);
ui::TextControl* box = stack->add(std::make_unique<ui::TextControl>("Resize me"));
box->set_width(200.0f);
box->set_height(120.0f);

ui::ResizeGripperControl* grip = stack->add(std::make_unique<ui::ResizeGripperControl>());
grip->set_horizontal_alignment(ui::Alignment::Trailing);
grip->on_drag_delta([box](ui::Point delta) {
    box->set_width(std::max(40.0f, box->width().value_or(0.0f) + delta.x));
    box->set_height(std::max(24.0f, box->height().value_or(0.0f) + delta.y));
});
window.set_content(std::move(stack));
```

## `ui::ResizeGripper`

A fixed-size corner drag handle. Builds a [ui::ResizeGripperControl](#uiresizegrippercontrol). [`.on_drag_delta`](#uiresizegripper-on_drag_delta) receives the (dx, dy) movement since its previous call. A caller typically passes it on to [GridControl::set_row_height()](grid.md#set_row_height) and set_column_width() on a grid it holds through [`.control`](#uiresizegripper-control). [ui::Splitter](splitter.md#uisplitter) is the single-axis version. It works with the mouse only and takes no focus.

Example: 
```cpp
using ui::operator""_dip;

ui::Control<ui::Grid> grid;

window.set_content(ui::Grid{
    .columns = {200_dip, ui::AutoSize},
    .rows    = {120_dip, ui::AutoSize},
    .control = grid,
    .content = {
        ui::Cell{.row = 0, .column = 0, .content = ui::Button{.text = "Resizable"}},
        ui::Cell{.row     = 1,
                 .column  = 1,
                 .content = ui::ResizeGripper{.on_drag_delta = [&](ui::Point delta)
                 {
                     grid->set_column_width(0, std::max(40.0f, grid->column_size(0) + delta.x));
                     grid->set_row_height(0, std::max(24.0f, grid->row_size(0) + delta.y));
                 }}},
    },
});
```

```cpp
}
```

## `ui::ResizeGripperControl`

Derives from `ui::Element`.

A fixed-size corner drag handle that reports two-axis deltas while dragged.

It draws three diagonal rows of dots anchored to its bottom-right corner, shows the diagonal resize cursor, and measures to a [`size()`](#size) square whatever it is offered. It resizes nothing itself. The app applies each (dx, dy) to whatever should grow, typically a [Grid](grid.md#uigrid) row and column or an element's explicit size. It works with the mouse only and never takes focus. For a single-axis pane splitter use [`Splitter`](splitter.md#uisplitter). [`ui::ResizeGripper`](#uiresizegripper) is the declarative form.

Example: 
```cpp
auto stack = std::make_unique<ui::StackControl>(ui::Orientation::Vertical);
```

### ResizeGripperControl

```cpp
ResizeGripperControl() = default
```

A 16 DIP gripper.

### size

```cpp
float size() const
```

The square's edge length in DIPs; 16 by default.

### set_size

```cpp
void set_size(float size)
```

Sets the edge length in DIPs and lays the gripper out again.

### on_drag_delta

```cpp
void on_drag_delta(Callback<void(Point delta)> handler)
```

Fired while the pointer drags, with the (dx, dy) movement since the previous call. Works like [SplitterControl::on_drag_delta](splitter.md#on_drag_delta), on both axes at once.

### dragging

```cpp
bool dragging() const
```

Whether a left-button drag is in progress. The dots draw at hover strength meanwhile.

### hovered

```cpp
bool hovered() const
```

Whether the pointer is over the gripper.

### cursor_at

```cpp
std::optional<CursorShape> cursor_at(Point) const override
```

The diagonal resize arrow, or none while disabled.

### automation_role

```cpp
AutomationRole automation_role() const override
```

Reported to screen readers as a Thumb.

### measure_override

```cpp
Size measure_override(Size available, const MeasureContext& context) const override
```

[`size()`](#size) x [`size()`](#size), regardless of `available`. The gripper is never focusable and has no keyboard resize.

### render_override

```cpp
void render_override(Renderer& renderer, const RenderContext& context) const override
```

Draws a triangle of dots (rows of one, two and three) in the corner, in the text color at reduced alpha.

### pointer_override

```cpp
bool pointer_override(const PointerEvent& e) override
```

A left press inside starts the drag. Each move then fires [`on_drag_delta()`](#on_drag_delta) until the button is released.

### enabled_changed

```cpp
void enabled_changed() override
```

[is_enabled()](../tree/element.md#is_enabled) flipped, through [set_enabled()](../tree/element.md#set_enabled) here or on an ancestor, or a move to another parent. Drop any press or hover state. The element is redrawn either way. No-op by default.
